final_candidates.decision_summary: Strongest escape phenotype with excellent structural compatibility and good sequence plausibility, making it the best balance of immune escape and probable receptor-binding preservation.
Strong escape and good structural compatibility with acceptable sequence plausibility; slightly less favored than E431K overall.
High escape and very strong structural compatibility, though modest sequence plausibility adds some uncertainty to in vivo receptor-binding preservation.

stop_reason.detail: Additional evidence is unlikely to change the final Top-3 given consistent multi-tool support and exhausted tool-call budget.

history.rationale: Conservative hydrophobic change at an epitope residue; could subtly alter the m102.4 interface while preserving receptor-binding architecture.
